en: Now begins the auspicious eulogy of Śrī Veṅkaṭeśa.
May there be auspiciousness unto Śrīnivāsa, who dwells on the Śrī Veṅkaṭa mountain, the beloved of Śrī, the treasure-house of welfare, and the refuge for those who seek his grace;
he whose eyes possess the playful grace of the tremulous brows of Lakṣmī as she gazes with amorous glances.
May there be auspiciousness for Veṅkaṭeśa, the eye of all the worlds.
(2) May there be auspiciousness for Veṅkaṭeśa, whose feet are the auspicious ornaments upon the very peak of the summit of Śrī Veṅkaṭādri, and who is the abode of all auspicious things. (3)
May there be auspiciousness for Veṅkaṭeśa, who, through the perfection of the beauty of all his limbs, eternally deludes the minds of all beings;
he who is eternal, faultless, and whose nature is truth, bliss, and consciousness. 4.
May there be auspiciousness unto the glorious Veṅkaṭeśa, the inner self of all.
May there be auspiciousness unto Veṅkaṭeśa, who is by his own nature the knower of all, the possessor of all power, the sovereign of all, easily accessible, and of excellent character.

I offer auspiciousness to Veṅkaṭeśa, the Supreme Reality, the Supreme Self, the Brahman who is the fulfillment of all desires. May he, who perceives without weariness the reality of the selves from beginningless time, [grant his grace]. 7.
Auspiciousness unto Veṅkaṭeśa, whose form is nectar that can never satiate!
(8) Auspiciousness unto the glorious Veṅkaṭeśa, who out of compassion generally points with his hand to the feet of men as their refuge! (9)
May there be auspiciousness for Veṅkaṭeśa, who sprinkles the universe with side-glances as cooling as the waves of the nectar-ocean of compassion;
salutations to him whose form brings forth the exquisite beauty of garlands, ornaments, garments, and weapons. 10.10-11a.
May there be auspiciousness for Veṅkaṭeśa, the pacifier of all suffering.
(11) May there be auspiciousness for Veṅkaṭeśa, who is detached from Śrī-Vaikuntha and who delights with Ramā on the bank of the Svāmipuṣkariṇī. (12)
May there be auspiciousness for Śrīnivāsa, who dwells in the heart of the venerable Sage Sundarajāmātṛ and who is the abode of all the worlds.
[This is said] by those led by my own teacher, who are intent on pronouncing blessings. 13.
And may there be auspiciousness for this [work] which has been honored by all the former teachers.
Thus ends the *Śrī-Veṅkaṭeśa-maṅgalāśāsanam*.
Oṃ tat sat.
